newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise sharply on Wall Street record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise sharply on Wall Street record.

text.p: French stocks rose on Wednesday in line with other European markets after Wall Street set a fresh record and the dollar advanced against European currencies.

The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 29.93 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,331.62 after forging through a zone of mild resistance around 2,325 points. The CAC-40 January futures contract rose 32 points to 2,337.
"It was a lovely trading session today, with lots of volume thanks to the recovery last night on Wall Street and most of all to the rise in the dollar," a trader said.
After backsliding for weeks on signs of volatility in the U.S. stockmarket, the CAC index is again poised to tackle its all-time record of 2,360.98 points.

But a big move looks unlikely ahead of the announcements of two key U.S. economic indicators on Thursday and Friday. "The bourse is totally in sync with Wall Street," said another trader. "The U.S. influence will be even more pronounced as we wait for producer prices on Thursday and jobs data on Friday."
Trading was a heavy 6.4 billion francs.

Shares in luxury goods group LVMH rose 3.11 percent to 1,460 francs. Dealers said they are expecting brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu to issue a favourable report on the group, taking into account the acquisition of U.S. duty free chain DFS.
U.S. antitrust authorities are expected to issue their decision on the deal soon, possibly next week.

Dassault Aviation shares finished up 7.42 percent at 1,259 francs, and Dassault Electronique's stock rose 5.38 percent to 490 francs on the latest developments in the restructuring of the French aerospace and defence industries.

A defence ministry official said state-owned Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation would be merged in the spring, and the group would subsequently be privatised. The government asked the privatisation commission to decide on the merger parities.

The newspaper La Tribune said the Aerospatiale-Dassault group may team up with engineering group Alcatel Alsthom to bid for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF. Alcatel shares rose 3.06 percent to 427.50 francs.
